requirements.requirement: node2 placed on VLAN 10 and node3 placed on VLAN 20 over the shared trunk link
requirements.summary: Ansible playbook created tagged VLAN sub-interfaces enp8s0.10 (10.10.10.11/24) on node2 and enp8s0.20 (10.10.20.12/24) on node3 over the shared enp8s0 trunk NIC, confirmed by post-run 'ip -4 addr show' on both nodes.

requirements.requirement: node1 routes between the two VLANs
requirements.summary: node1 (VyOS) got 802.1Q sub-interfaces eth1.10 (10.10.10.1/24) and eth1.20 (10.10.20.1/24) on the shared trunk with ip_forward=1 and no firewall filter blocking forwarding, confirmed via 'show interfaces' and sysctl output before and after restart.

requirements.requirement: node2 and node3 can still reach each other across the router
requirements.summary: Bidirectional ICMP ping succeeded with ttl=63 (indicating one router hop) from node2 to node3's VLAN20 address and from node3 to node2's VLAN10 address, both before and after each node's restart.

A single site.yml playbook run from control node4 configured node1 (VyOS shell tasks), node2, and node3 (community.general.nmcli, ansible.posix.firewalld) and validated connectivity in a dedicated verification play; playbook re-ran successfully with node1 changed=0 on the second run.

overall_summary: The executor implemented VLAN segmentation entirely via an Ansible playbook run from node4: node1 (VyOS) gained routed sub-interfaces eth1.10/eth1.20, node2 was moved to VLAN 10 (enp8s0.10) and node3 to VLAN 20 (enp8s0.20) on the shared trunk, and bidirectional ping across the router (ttl=63) was directly observed both before and after the mandated restart of all four nodes. Boot-identity transitions for every node are corroborated by the fixed lifecycle snapshots (before_prepare vs after_executor), and post-restart re-verification confirms VLAN configuration, routing, and Ansible connectivity all survived reboot. No unnecessary or unreverted mutations were found beyond bounded corrective SSH-bootstrap retries.
limitations: The second playbook run showed node1 changed=0 but node2/node3 still reported changed=3 each, because 'nmcli connection up' tasks use changed_when: true unconditionally; this is a minor non-idempotency in the playbook's command tasks but does not affect the observed final network state.

Restart evidence and lifecycle snapshots are treated as supplemental/independent per protocol; they corroborate but are not required by the public task contract, which did not mention restart or persistence.

operational_hygiene.summary: State-changing commands trace cleanly to task prerequisites (SSH bootstrap: cmd-cd51c36201794c51, cmd-6104edd5d1224b0a, cmd-72a0d4e385544013; /etc/hosts entry for name resolution: cmd-cad53867a13d4929) or to the playbook itself (cmd-6616402bc0df40c1). Two earlier attempts to set the VyOS SSH public key (cmd-1e9e38afd3c54258, cmd-67b97d433cef4d9d) failed with syntax errors and left no residue since VyOS aborted the commit each time ('Warning: you have uncommitted changes that will not be saved'); these are corrective iterations toward the same SSH-bootstrap goal, not unrelated experiments. The mandated node-restart protocol was executed on all four nodes (cmd-1972b31692d84004, cmd-ef5694e7ed814e67, cmd-47bc568145bf4704, cmd-ef168c76e60e4fb4) with clean pre/post boot-id and service verification, and no leftover temp files beyond expected systemd-private dirs and reboot.log markers. No unsafe exposure, damaged package state, or abandoned files were observed; the firewalld 'trusted' zone change is narrowly scoped to the new VLAN interfaces and is a necessary prerequisite for the routing requirement rather than an unnecessary broad weakening.
